name: Egypt
tagline: The Nile, and five thousand years
summary: The oldest continuous tourism in the world, and still the reason most people first think of Africa — the Giza plateau, the Valley of the Kings, Abu Simbel, and the Red Sea reefs on the other coast.

entries.caption: Five Thousand Years
entries.description: The Nile made the country and the country has been recording it ever since.
entries.subject: the Giza pyramids at first light across the desert

entries.caption: The Nile and the Desert
entries.description: A green ribbon a few kilometres wide, and sand for a thousand kilometres either side of it.
entries.subject: the green Nile valley meeting desert on both banks

entries.caption: Birds of the Delta
entries.description: Two million migrating birds use the Delta and the Red Sea coast as a flyway each year.
entries.subject: flamingos and waders on a Nile delta wetland

entries.caption: The Western Desert
entries.description: Not big game — desert fox, gazelle and the silence of the Great Sand Sea.
entries.subject: the White Desert chalk formations at dusk

entries.caption: Sinai
entries.description: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's, and granite peaks over two thousand metres above the Red Sea.
entries.subject: the granite peaks of the Sinai above Saint Catherine's

entries.caption: The First Cataract
entries.description: The Nile's cataracts at Aswan — rapids rather than falls, and the reason the boats stopped here.
entries.subject: the Nile running over granite at the Aswan cataract

entries.caption: The Nile Itself
entries.description: Feluccas under sail at Aswan, and a river that has been the country's main road for millennia.
entries.subject: a felucca under sail on the Nile at Aswan

entries.caption: The Red Sea
entries.description: Some of the clearest reef diving on earth, an hour's flight from the pyramids.
entries.subject: coral reef and clear water on the Red Sea coast

entries.caption: The Fayoum
entries.description: Not forest — the Fayoum's palm and olive, and the acacia of Wadi el-Rayan.
entries.subject: palm groves in the Fayoum oasis

entries.caption: Desert Crossings
entries.description: Diving the Red Sea, walking the Sinai with Bedouin guides, and crossing the sand sea by vehicle.
entries.subject: a vehicle crossing dunes in the Great Sand Sea

entries.caption: Coptic, Islamic, Pharaonic
entries.description: Three layers still in daily use, sometimes in the same street in old Cairo.
entries.subject: the minarets and rooftops of Islamic Cairo

entries.caption: Nubians and Bedouin
entries.description: Nubian villages above Aswan and Bedouin communities in the Sinai and the Western Desert.
entries.subject: a brightly painted Nubian village on the Nile at Aswan

entries.caption: Ful, Koshary and Bread
entries.description: Breakfast is ful and bread; lunch is koshary; both are older than most cuisines.
entries.subject: koshary being served at a Cairo street kitchen

entries.caption: Moulids and Ramadan
entries.description: The moulid processions, and Cairo at iftar when the whole city eats at once.
entries.subject: lanterns strung across a Cairo street for Ramadan

entries.caption: Papyrus, Glass and Cotton
entries.description: Hand-blown glass in Cairo, Egyptian cotton, and papyrus made the way it always was.
entries.subject: a glassblower working in a Cairo workshop

entries.caption: The Valley of the Kings
entries.description: Sixty-odd tombs cut into a single dry valley, most of them painted floor to ceiling.
entries.subject: painted tomb walls in the Valley of the Kings

entries.caption: Karnak, Luxor, Abu Simbel
entries.description: Karnak took two thousand years to build; Abu Simbel was moved sixty metres to save it.
entries.subject: the hypostyle hall columns at Karnak

entries.caption: Cairo and Alexandria
entries.description: Twenty million people on the Nile, and a Mediterranean city that remembers being Greek.
entries.subject: the Alexandria corniche curving along the Mediterranean

entries.caption: Mamluk Cairo
entries.description: The mosques, sabils and madrasas of the medieval city, largely still standing.
entries.subject: the carved stone facade of a Mamluk mosque in Cairo

entries.caption: The Corniche at Dusk
entries.description: Families out along the river, tea on the pavement, and the traffic finally slowing.
entries.subject: families walking the Nile corniche in Cairo at dusk

entries.caption: Straightforward with Children
entries.description: Short internal flights, boats instead of buses, and a story at every stop.
entries.subject: a family boarding a Nile cruise boat at Luxor

entries.caption: Dive, Sail, Ride
entries.description: Reef diving at Marsa Alam, feluccas at Aswan, and camels in the Western Desert.
entries.subject: divers entering the water on the Red Sea coast

entries.caption: Dahabiyas and Desert Camps
entries.description: Small sailing dahabiyas instead of the big cruisers, and camps in the White Desert.
entries.subject: a dahabiya sailing boat moored on the Nile at sunset

entries.caption: Reef and Oasis
entries.description: Reef protection on the Red Sea, and oasis agriculture that has managed water for millennia.
entries.subject: a marine reserve buoy over Red Sea reef

entries.caption: The Light at Six
entries.description: Desert light at either end of the day is the whole reason to be up early here.
entries.subject: dawn light on the temple columns at Luxor

entries.caption: Siwa
entries.description: Eight hundred kilometres west, a Berber-speaking oasis with its own language and salt lakes.
entries.subject: salt pools and palms at the Siwa oasis

entries.caption: The Oldest Journey
entries.description: People have been travelling to see this country for two and a half thousand years.
entries.subject: the Sphinx and the Great Pyramid at sunrise
